title.en: Measure voltage, period and frequency with a CRO
Find frequency ratio and phase with Lissajous figures

say.en: The CRO screen is a grid of boxes. Count how many boxes a waveform covers, multiply by the knob setting, and you have its voltage and frequency. In this lesson: Measure voltage, period and frequency with a CRO.
Find frequency ratio and phase with Lissajous figures.
Describe the function generator.

body.en: The screen is marked in divisions (usually 10 across and 8 up). *Voltage*: $V_{pp}$ = (vertical divisions, peak to peak) × (volts/div setting); then $V_m = V_{pp}/2$ and $V_{rms} = V_m/\sqrt{2}$ for a sine wave. Time: the period T = (horizontal divisions for one cycle) × (time/div setting), and the frequency f = 1/T. The CRO can also show the shape of a waveform, its rise time and the phase between two signals on a dual-trace screen.

points.en: V_rms = V_pp/(2√2) for a sine wave

narration.en: Peak-to-peak voltage is the number of vertical divisions times the volts per division. The period is the horizontal divisions times the time per division, and the frequency is one over the period.
narration.kn: ಶಿಖರದಿಂದ-ಶಿಖರ ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ = ಲಂಬ ವಿಭಾಗಗಳು × ವೋಲ್ಟ್ ಪ್ರತಿ ವಿಭಾಗ. ಆವರ್ತ ಕಾಲ = ಅಡ್ಡ ವಿಭಾಗಗಳು × ಕಾಲ ಪ್ರತಿ ವಿಭಾಗ; ಆವೃತ್ತಿ = 1/ಆವರ್ತ ಕಾಲ.

say.en: Peak-to-peak voltage is the number of vertical divisions times the volts per division. The period is the horizontal divisions times the time per division, and the frequency is one over the period. V pp equals divisions times V over div.
say.kn: ಶಿಖರದಿಂದ-ಶಿಖರ ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ = ಲಂಬ ವಿಭಾಗಗಳು times ವೋಲ್ಟ್ ಪ್ರತಿ ವಿಭಾಗ. ಆವರ್ತ ಕಾಲ equals ಅಡ್ಡ ವಿಭಾಗಗಳು times ಕಾಲ ಪ್ರತಿ ವಿಭಾಗ; ಆವೃತ್ತಿ = 1/ಆವರ್ತ ಕಾಲ.

say.en: T equals divisions times time/div; f equals 1 over T.
V rms equals V pp over 2 the square root of 2 for a sine wave.

title.en: Reading voltage and frequency on a CRO

say.en: The screen has a grid of divisions: ten across and eight up.
Here is a sine wave. Peak to peak it covers six divisions, and one cycle spans four divisions.
Multiply by the control settings. At 2 volts per division the peak-to-peak voltage is 12 volts. At 5 milliseconds per division the period is 20 milliseconds, so the frequency is 50 hertz.
With signals on both X and Y plates we get a Lissajous figure. Count where it touches a horizontal line and a vertical line: f y over f x is horizontal touches over vertical touches.

title.en: Lissajous figures and the function generator

body.en: With the time base off, one signal goes to the X plates and another to the Y plates. The pattern is a Lissajous figure. Its shape gives the frequency ratio: $f_y/f_x$ = (number of points touching a horizontal tangent)/(number touching a vertical tangent). For equal frequencies the figure shows the phase: a line for 0° or 180°, an ellipse in between with $\sin\phi$ = (Y-intercept)/(maximum Y), and a circle for 90° with equal amplitudes. A *function generator* supplies sine, square and triangular waves whose frequency and amplitude can be set, for testing circuits.

narration.en: A Lissajous figure compares two signals. The ratio of horizontal to vertical tangent points gives f y over f x, and the shape of an ellipse gives the phase difference.
narration.kn: ಲಿಸಾಜೂ ಆಕೃತಿ ಎರಡು ಸಂಕೇತಗಳನ್ನು ಹೋಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಅಡ್ಡ ಮತ್ತು ಲಂಬ ಸ್ಪರ್ಶಕ ಬಿಂದುಗಳ ಅನುಪಾತ fy/fx ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ; ದೀರ್ಘವೃತ್ತದ ಆಕಾರ ಹಂತ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: A Lissajous figure compares two signals. The ratio of horizontal to vertical tangent points gives f y over f x, and the shape of an ellipse gives the phase difference. f y over f x equals horizontal tangencies divided by vertical tangencies.

problem.en: A sine wave on a CRO is 6 divisions peak to peak and one cycle spans 4 divisions. The settings are 2 V/div and 5 ms/div. Find V_pp, V_m, V_rms and the frequency.

answer.en: V_pp = 12 V, V_m = 6 V, V_rms ≈ 4.24 V, f = 50 Hz

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A sine wave on a CRO is 6 divisions peak to peak and one cycle spans 4 divisions. The settings are 2 V/div and 5 ms/div. Find V_pp, V_m, V_rms and the frequency.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A sine wave on a CRO is 6 divisions peak to peak and one cycle spans 4 divisions. The settings are 2 V over div and 5 ms over div. Find V pp, V m, V rms and the frequency.
V pp equals 6 times 2 equals 12 volts, so V m equals 6 volts.
V rms equals V m/ the square root of 2 equals 6 over 1.414 is approximately 4.24 volts.
T equals 4 times 5 milliseconds equals 20 milliseconds, so f equals 1 over 0.020 equals 50 hertz.
So the answer is V pp equals 12 volts, V m equals 6 volts, V rms is approximately 4.24 volts, f equals 50 hertz.

problem.en: A Lissajous figure touches a horizontal tangent at 3 points and a vertical tangent at 2 points. The X input is 400 Hz. Find the Y frequency.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A Lissajous figure touches a horizontal tangent at 3 points and a vertical tangent at 2 points. The X input is 400 Hz. Find the Y frequency.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A Lissajous figure touches a horizontal tangent at 3 points and a vertical tangent at 2 points. The X input is 400 hertz. Find the Y frequency.
f y over f x equals horizontal tangencies divided by vertical tangencies equals 3 over 2.
f y equals 1.5 times 400 equals 600 hertz.
So the answer is 600 hertz.

body.en: Y is the vertical plate, and a vertical signal makes the figure bump against a horizontal line. So f_y goes with the horizontal tangent count: f_y/f_x = horizontal touches/vertical touches.
